grades.quote: However, the processes running on the other two virtual machines will remain isolated, so long as the ESX Server software continues to do its job.
grades.reason: Provides background on VMM-enforced isolation, but does not explain privileged-instruction interception.

grades.quote: The VMM runs in kernel mode. When the underlying processor executes instructions from one of the virtual machines, on the other hand, it does so in user mode. That way, the VMM is in complete control and can protect the virtual machines from one another.
grades.reason: Directly explains that interception preserves monitor control and guest isolation, then describes emulating legitimate guest OS operations.

grades.quote: The first is to improve the speed of instruction emulation in a trap handler, partly by allowing the handler to skip loading the trapping instruction from memory, and partly by obviating some of the work of decoding and executing the instruction.
grades.reason: Provides auxiliary information about trap-handler instruction emulation, but not why privileged guest operations require interception.
